 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 29-09-2024 at about 12-45 pm., the petitioner as a pedestrian, was walking in old outer ring road, Kottigepalya, Bangalore and when he reached near Vokkaligara Sangha Vidyasamsthe, Balaji Hardware and Paints, Bangalore city, at that time the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02/KX-6068 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner, result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Unity Life line Hospital wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to True life Specialty Hospital, wherein admitted as an inpatient.

So far, the petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, nourishment food, conveyance,
transportation etc.,
3.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was doing plumbing work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the permanent disability, the petitioner is not in a position to do the said work as earlier and undergone tremendous pain, mental shock, agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In response to the notice, the respondent no.1 did not appear before this tribunal and remained absent Hence he was placed ex-parte.
5. The respondent no.2 /the insurer of motorcycle bearing Reg/No.KA-02-KX-6068
has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 contends that the rider of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license and that the alleged accident was due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner alone, who was trying to cross the main road without having proper look out of the vehicular movement and suddenly came to the middle of the road in order to cross the road, even there is no provision for pedestrian to cross near the place of accident, hence petitioner is also the tort feasor.

The respondent no.2 further contended that the insured vehicle was not involved in the accident, that the petitioner, in collusion with the Srinivasa vs Vtech Careers on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58910399/
2 jurisdictional police and owner of the vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gain.
6. Heard the arguments on both sides.
7. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed::-
ISSUES 1.

sentences.text:
Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 29-09-2024 at about 12-45 p.m on Old outer ring road, near Vokkaligara Sangha Vidyasamsthe, Balaji Hardware and Paints, Kottigepalya,
Bangalore-560091due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02/KX-6068?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award?
8. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and one witness is examined as PW.2 and marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
The respondent no.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

Issue No.1: - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place, on 29-09-2024 at about 12-45 pm., when the petitioner as a pedestrian, was walking in old outer ring road,
Kottigepalya, Bangalore and when he reached near Vokkaligara Sangha Vidyasamsthe, Balaji Hardware and Paints, Bangalore city, at that time motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02/KX-6068 (hereinafter called the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner, result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

The P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as F.I.R, Complaint, Spot mahazar, Spot sketch, Wound certificate, Notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV Act and reply given thereon, IMV report and Charge sheet etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by petitioner's son by name Umesh.S, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No.144/2024 of Kamakshipalya Traffic Srinivasa vs Vtech Careers on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58910399/
3 Police Station for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(b) of BNS, 2023.

sentences.text:
After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(b) of BNS.
13.

So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, it is vehemently argued by the Learned counsel for respondent no.2 that at the place of accident there was no pedestrian crossing and it is a ring road where there are three lanes on either side and the petitioner in his attempt to cross the road stepped in to the road at the place where there is no zebra crossing hence petitioner too has contributed negligence.

14. In the light of the contention taken by the Learned counsel for respondent no.2 if spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 60 feet and there is center median in between the road of the width of 30 feet each.
The offending vehicle was proceeding from Kottigepalya towards BDA complex.
It runs North to South direction and petitioner was crossing the road from East to West direction.
It is one way road ie., leading to BDA Complex.

Though the Learned counsel for respondent no.2 has submitted that the petitioner was crossing the road at the place where there is no zebra crossing, but no single suggestion was posed to the PW.1 during his cross examination about the PW.1 crossing the road at the place where there is no zebra crossing.

Further it is nowhere the case of the respondent no.2 that in the said road there was zebra crossing at a short distance from the place of accident and the petitioner instead of using the zebra crossing has tried to cross the road at some other place and met with an accident.
If the sketch is perused, the spot of accident is on the extreme right side of Kottigepalya - BDA Complex road ie., on the extreme eastern side of the said road.
When the width of the road is nearly 30 feet there was no necessity for the rider of the motorcycle to take his vehicle on the extreme right side of the road.

Had the rider of the motorcycle ride his vehicle on the left side of the road or in the middle of the road,
this accident would not have occurred.

The mere fact that the petitioner has stepped in to the road,
on that ground alone it cannot be said that he too has contributed negligence.
If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the negligence on the part of the petitioner cannot be made out.
Further the respondent no.2 has not taken steps to examine the rider of the offending vehicle.
There is no rebuttal evidence from the side of respondent no.2 so far as this material point is concerned.

Hence,
the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents placed on record it can be said that the rider of the motorcycle alone is the cause for the accident.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are marked at Ex.P4 and P8.
On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient from 30-09- 2024 to 04-10-2024 at True life Specialty Hospital, Bangalore, for a period of 5 days.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained two injuries which are grievous in nature.
16. Dr. Ramesh .B., Orthopedic surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, is examined as Pw2 and through him OPD Card & x-ray are got marked as Ex.P13 to 14.
P.W.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 24-06-2025 for disability assessment.

PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has Srinivasa vs Vtech Careers on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58910399/
4 suffered permanent physical disability on right lower limb at 32% and to the whole body at 16% and that petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implant.
17.
If the cross examination of PW.2 is carefully perused, PW.2 is not a treated doctor.
He has not verifiy any document for the follow up treatment taken by the petitioner .

As per the evidence of PW.2 the implants are in situ and the implant and alignment are in proper position and that it is after 12 weeks of the surgery, the petitioner was in a position to walk without any support but with some difficulty.
According to the PW.2 the fracture injury is united but he pleaded ignorance as to when it was united.
As observed supra, the PW.2 having assessed the disability on right lower limb at 32%, assessed the disability on whole body at 16%.

As per the judgment reported in 2014 (4)
Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk, the normal rule would be disability in the lower limb would be 1/3rd of the particular limb.

2014 (4)
Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the disability on the whole body would have to be 14% but because of the line of evidence given by the PW.2, this court inclines to consider the disability of petitioner on whole body at 10%.
18. Considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
19. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained two grievous injuries.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
20. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced medical bill for Rs.2,17,057/-, as per Ex.P10.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.2,17,057/-
21.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 59 years and he was doing plumbing work and was earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, year of accident and the place of residence of the petitioner considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
22.
The petitioner has sustained two grievous injuries and has taken treatment for 5 days as inpatient in True life Speciality hospital, Bangalore.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of three months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m. for 3 months.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.49,500/- (16,500X3)
towards loss of income during the laid down period .
23. From the evidence of Pw.1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at True life Specialty Hospital Limited, Bangalore.

entities.text: True life Specialty Hospital Limited, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further for 5 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.

He has taken nourishment and needs further Srinivasa vs Vtech Careers on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58910399/
5 nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.20,000/- taking into consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
24. The petitioner has contended that, he was aged about 59 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P12/Aadhar card of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 12-05-1965 that means he was aged about 60 years.
Hence considering the copy of Aadhaar card this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 60 years at the time of accident.

25. So taking into consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.16,500/- p.m and if 10% of loss of earning capacity is considered and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 60 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 56 to 60 is '09'.
So by applying the multiplier '09' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.1,78,200/- (i.e., 16,500 x 10% x 9 x12 )-.
Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,78,200/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
26. PW.2 has stated that petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implant.
The PW.2 has not stated the estimated cost of future surgery and has not given estimation.
Hence, this court inclines to award future medical expenses only to the tune of Rs.30,000/-.
27. The petitioner at his age of 60 years has suffered grievous injury which definitely would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of comfort and amenities, thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/-
 2. Medical expenses Rs. 2,17,057/-
 3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 49,500/-
 laid up period  4. Towards Conveyance, Attendant
charges and nourishing food

5. Future Loss of Income Rs. 1,78,200/-
 6. Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000/-
 7. Loss of amenities and discomfort Rs. 30,000/-
Total Rs

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,94,727/- (Rupees Five Lakh Ninety Four Thousand Seven Hundred Twenty Seven only).
Srinivasa vs Vtech Careers on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58910399/
6 28.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the rider of the offending vehicle had driving license to ride the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question were valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2, this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly, Issue No. 2 is answered.
29. Issue No.3: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER  The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.5,94,757/- + cost of Rs.1,500/- imposed vide order on IA No.III & IV.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.5,96,257/- (Rupees Five Lakh Ninety Six Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Seven only).

After deducting cost of Rs.1,500/- and future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.30,000/- balance sum of Rs.5,64,757/- shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
